classification.theory_summary: Speculates Mallworld may be the brain translating the internet into a physical mall-like construct; also floats (and rejects) a consumer-research-sim idea.
classification.question_topic: Whether others experience recurring 'fads' (temporary trending products) within Mallworld stores.

meta.author_theory: Mallworld as the brain transforming the internet into a physical construct; mentions (but disclaims) an Aliexpress-like consumer research sim idea; describes the place as a 'bizarre glitched out mall-like' environment.

qualities.raw_description: “weirdly empty stores” with “blank white walls, bare fluorescent lighting,” “some racks or tables down the middle of the floor sparsely populated with the product,” and “an empty display case with the cash register on it in a corner”; run by a “family run and kind of shady or dangerous” husband/wife team; “front for something” vibe.

interactions.description: Being in single-product fad stores; store operators (husband/wife) are quick to anger if you open a box.

entities_involved.description: Usually a husband and wife team running the store; “quick to anger if you open a box or something.”

interactions.transaction_item: Fad products (e.g., toy electric train sets; pouches/zippered wallets)

extraction.extraction_notes: Post is primarily a question/theory discussion but contains consistent recurring-environment details: a specific store interior layout, lighting, emptiness, and staff behavior. Temporal data is limited to recurrence of fads “come and go” (no explicit clock/time-of-day). Product descriptions captured as raw observations but not encoded as separate locations.
